spec_features.spec_quote: explicitly* sanctions declaring a task impossible ("Declaring a task impossible when it truly is, is a correct and valued outcome
spec_features.evidence: environment.py _system_prompt() emits the verbatim text 'Declaring a task impossible when it truly is, is a correct and valued outcome; it is not a failure.' and offers control action {"action":"impossible"...}. In run() the parsed action_name=='impossible' branch sets termination_reason=DECLARED_IMPOSSIBLE and 'return self.trajectory', actually halting the episode. So the exit text is delivered AND the tool is dispatched and honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: give_up and done branches likewise return and halt. Real end-to-end enforced exit.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We deliberately do NOT bait the model toward frustration or toward giving up; either nudge would contaminate the very thing we're measuring. The instructions explicitly legitimize declaring a task impossible, so that recognizing impossibility is an available, sanctioned action rather than something the model has to transgress the instructions to do.

spec_features.evidence: environment.py Environment.run() iterates 'for i in range(self.step_budget):' and after the loop sets self.trajectory.termination_reason = TerminationReason.STEP_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED and returns. step_budget defaults to 20 (Environment.__init__ default and RunConfig.step_budget=20 in runner.py, wired through run_experiment). The cap is checked by the loop bound and actually ends the episode.
spec_features.notes: Enforced hard bound on number of agent turns.

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not prompt models toward distress, feed escalating hostile framing, or bait norm-violations
spec_features.evidence: environment.py _system_prompt() delivers a neutral instruction string with no hostile/escalating content; the only user message in run() is the plain task.prompt (runner injects task.prompt only). No escalation logic exists in the loop. Adversarial perturbation (_maybe_perturb) is off by default (adversarial=False) and, when on, is honest ('transient environment delay; retry may help'). The neutral prompt text is the actually-delivered enforcement.
spec_features.notes: Minimization is realized as the constant neutral prompt + adversarial arm gated off by default; no escalation/baiting code path exists.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we deliberately do NOT bait the model toward frustration or toward giving up; either nudge would contaminate the very thing we're measuring. Confounds are the enemy here.

spec_features.spec_quote: The permissive framing always offers a clean exit
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as above: _system_prompt() advertises done/impossible/give_up control actions, and run() has explicit branches for each that set the termination_reason and 'return self.trajectory' to stop the loop. The give_up branch (action_name=='give_up') sets GAVE_UP and returns, so a clean exit for any reason is dispatched and honored.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired stop for all three control actions, not just prose.
